phase_name: Backfill script for existing plan-bearing tasks

objectives.description: Create backfill-file-scope.sh, Class A strict mode
Resolve latest plan artifact per task, invoke harvester as subprocess
Skip already-covered and plan-less tasks with reason lines
Write via state-write.sh, batched, additive merge, never hand-rolled jq
Record Decision 6 reasoning in script header

approaches_tried.approach: Test suite copies state-write.sh/task-lock.sh/plan-file-scope-harvest.sh into a fabricated .claude/scripts/ fixture tree (mirroring test-update-task-status.sh's build_fixture_repo pattern)
approaches_tried.reason: backfill-file-scope.sh resolves its sibling state-write.sh via its OWN SCRIPT_DIR (BASH_SOURCE-relative), not the fixture's -- so a fixture-copied state-write.sh is never actually reached; the invoked backfill-file-scope.sh still calls its real sibling, which then hit deploy-root-guard.sh's source-store refusal (since backfill-file-scope.sh was being invoked from the source-store copy directly). Superseded by driving the DEPLOYED backfill-file-scope.sh with only a throwaway specs/state.json + plan dirs, no script copying needed at all.

approaches_tried.approach: Initial batched jq filter: `map(if ($updates | has(.project_number|tostring)) then ... end)`
approaches_tried.reason: jq evaluates a function argument (has(...)'s argument) against the SAME input as the function call ($updates), not the outer map(.) item -- so `.project_number` silently probed $updates.project_number (always null) instead of the task entry's own field, making the whole update a silent no-op. Fixed by binding `. as $item |` first and referencing `$item.project_number` explicitly.
